newsitem.title: EGYPT: Palestinians vow to pressure Israel at conference.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians vow to pressure Israel at conference.

text.p: Palestinian leaders vowed to use the remaining two days of a Middle East economic conference as a weapon in their negotiations with Israel.

The first day of the Middle East/North Africa Conference in Cairo saw a flurry of diplomatic activity with U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher meeting Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

Christopher said he believed an Israel-PLO agreement on Hebron was "close at hand" but his spokesman later warned against expecting a deal in the next few days on implementing a long overdue Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank town.
Nabil Shaath, the Palestinian minister of planning and international cooperation, said Israel would be under pressure to honour its agreements signed with the Palestinians.

"We want this conference to say to Israel 'Look around you, there are 10,000 businesssmen here, talking about cooperation and development...but look behind you, if you don't carry out the commitments you made, you won't get any of it'," he told a news conference.

The region's political problems also spilled over into one of the conference's first panel sessions, with Palestinians accusing Israel's right-wing government of strangling their economy and hindering regional cooperation.

"We have been unable to do any substantial business with the rest of the world and also with our neighbours Jordan and Egypt," said Maher Masri, Palestinian economy and trade minister, referring to Israeli closures of self-rule areas.
"We cannot survive under such circumstances...poverty never produces peace," he said.
Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy came to the conference for the day to meet Christopher but did not address the meeting, which he appeared to criticise in remarks to reporters.

"This conference which is taking place in Cairo is different from previous conferences... which had a political dimension and which included Israel in the preparations and the substance," he said. "This conference is an Egyptian economic conference."
With the politicians leaving Cairo on Tuesday, there was a chance the conference could get down to the business of doing business in the volatile Middle East.
There were fears, however, that Arab executives may cold shoulder their Israeli counterparts although Palestinian leaders denied there was any organised boycott.

"We didn't ask anyone to boycott anyone. We came to this conference with a clear conscience, to tell the world we are going on with the peace process. But definitely there is a feeling of anger among the delegations," said Shaath.
Pressed on whether there was an organised boycott of Israel, he said: "As far as I know it is spontaneous."
An Israeli official at the conference said many Arab executives had already visited business desks run by Israel's export institute.
